title: Learning Lab Agreement — Eligibility and Participation
content: A participant, the Office and a relevant agency or eligible governmental entity may enter a regulatory mitigation agreement (RMA) or joint interpretation agreement (JIA). An RMA can allow a specified use subject to a cure period or similar remedy, reduced civil fines, or other tailored terms. Each participant remains subject to requirements outside any express waiver or modification. A JIA clarifies how a provision of state law or rule applies to the technology. The initial demonstration period may last up to twelve months. The participant may request a twelve-month extension at least thirty days before expiry, and the Office must grant or deny the request before expiry. The Office may grant up to two extensions. Counterparties include OAIP plus the relevant state agency (or the judiciary, a state-funded higher or public education institution, or a political subdivision under HB 320), and participants must satisfy five statutory eligibility prongs.
source_citation: Utah SB 149 (2024 General Session), Governor Signed March 13, 2024

The PubLedge JIA and its 30-minute re-display term remain an unpublished draft and are not statutory terms.
Utah HB 452 section 13-72a-203 uses a seven-day interaction condition rather than the draft JIA 30-minute resumption condition.

The disclose-genai-on-first-session obligation id and name still say 'first session'; its text was corrected in a separate receipt.
This is selected-clause source consistency, not a complete current-law/applicability or agency-interpretation certification. No human verification date renewed.
